question: Does keeping the real pair-edge correspondence of the key-centred induced local graph change performance and generalisation under an identical interaction body?

recipe.selection: strict < on valid MAE; ties keep the earlier epoch
recipe.init: from scratch (no SSL encoder, no supervised P3/DCC checkpoint)

amendment.reason: The frozen 2500-epoch schedule was 780,000 updates, i.e. 16.7x the 46,800 updates of the DCC-L reference recipe (600 epochs x 78 updates at batch 128). Budget alignment must be in updates, not epochs. 600 x 312 = 187,200 updates keeps 4x the reference optimisation budget while making the absolute valid number comparable: at the old schedule the cosine LR was still ~1.9e-3 at epoch 300, so no mid-run number could be compared with a converged DCC-L run. Warmup is held at the same 2% of training (12/600 epochs = 3,744 updates vs 50/2500 = 15,600) so the warmup fraction is unchanged. Nothing else in the recipe, model, data or gates changes.

model.norm: AdaRMSNorm (RMS + DiT-style adaptive scale/shift, no BatchNorm)
model.pe: shared static RRWP stem (k=0..20, sin/cos frequencies), never updated per layer
model.urpe: not implemented (paper alignment could not be verified offline)
model.token_set: one token per undirected physical bond
model.local_object: full typed induced graph on {u,v} U N(u) U N(v), roles (dist(i,u), dist(i,v)), root directions averaged
model.null_arm: every pair i<j receives the object-level 4-class frequency vector instead of its own edge class
model.readout: sum h_b / ref_bonds, sum h_b^2 / ref_bonds, sum AtomEmb / ref_atoms, 4 count scalars, frozen global33

budget.depth_rule: 12 blocks; if the parameter audit exceeds 500k, reduce to 10, then 8, decided only by the audit
